title: Trees with exactly three main eigenvalues
summary: An eigenvalue of a graph is called main if its eigenspace is not orthogonal to the all-ones vector. Introduced by Cvetković in the early 1970s and systematically studied by Rowlinson and others, graphs with exactly one or two main eigenvalues are now well understood. However, the classification of graphs with precisely three main eigenvalues remains a challenging open problem in spectral graph theory.
